strings.index.title.73: FireRatShader — The single shader that does everything
strings.index.p.62: The single shader that does everything — for every Unity project. Hundreds of effects, lighting models, and tools in one master shader per render pipeline. Built for VR, mobile, and desktop.
strings.index.p.66: Most shaders force you to choose: feature-rich but slow, or fast but limited. FireRatShader refuses that compromise.
strings.index.p.14: True 100% feature parity between Built-in (BRP) and URP. Same properties, same inspector, same look. Switch render pipelines without rebuilding your materials.
strings.index.p.16: Optimized for Meta Quest, SteamVR, and standalone Android. The Material Lock optimizer physically strips unused passes and dead variants at lock time — what ships is exactly what you use.
strings.index.p.18: Four emission layers, spectrum and waveform visualizers, raymarched fractals, and dozens of effects all driven by AudioLink. Test audio reactivity without entering Play Mode.
strings.index.p.20: 14 surface styles, 5 lighting models, shell fur, decals, dissolve, glitch, refraction, outlines, parallax, VAT — 800+ properties, every one keyword-gated so disabled features cost zero GPU time.
strings.index.span.22: Standard PBR, Toon, MatCap, Skin, Hair, Eye, Galaxy, Crystal, Glitter, Grid, Psychedelic, 3D Fractal, Triplanar, Iridescence
strings.index.span.24: Unlit, Basic, Toon, Stylized PBR, Standard PBR — switchable per material
strings.index.span.26: 1–8 extruded layers with wind, gravity, noise masking, and tip thinning
strings.index.span.28: Normal/metallic/smoothness overrides, 5 blend modes, AudioLink reactivity
strings.index.span.30: HDR colors, scrolling, masking, AudioLink frequency bands, and bloom luminance clamp
strings.index.span.32: EQ bars, oscilloscope, radial spectrum, 2D waterfall, polar ring, and stereo X-Y
strings.index.span.34: UV, world, local, screen, planar, spherical, cylindrical, triplanar, panosphere, polar
strings.index.span.36: Dedicated stencil buffer, world/local/screen width spaces, color map, and animation
strings.index.span.38: Noise, wave, spherical, glitch — with edge color, emission, and AudioLink reactivity
strings.index.span.40: Adjustable step count, linear search interpolation, with UV-space safety guards
strings.index.span.42: JSON translation packs with hot-reload, English fallback, language selector toolbar
strings.index.span.44: Strips unused passes, bakes keywords as #defines, rewrites includes for standalone builds
strings.index.p.70: FireRatShader ships with a built-in performance system so the same material scales from desktop VR down to low-end mobile.
strings.index.td.12: Disables distortion, parallax, and all Medium restrictions
strings.index.p.72: FireRatShader is a commercial Unity asset. The shader itself is not included in this repository — only the documentation, marketing material, and community language packs.
strings.docs.index.p.1216: Welcome to the documentation for FireRatShader. This shader is designed to be a powerful but efficient Uber shader that works in VR, Android, Mobile, Windows, and Unity 6 across both render pipelines: Built-in Render Pipeline Universal Render Pipeline
strings.docs.index.p.1217: Both pipeline versions share the exact same 828 properties, inspector layout, and feature sets in 100% lockstep parity.
strings.docs.index.p.1218: Use the navigation on the left to jump to a specific feature section. Each section corresponds to a foldout in the material inspector.
strings.docs.index.p.1220: The FireRat Shader Avatar Setup tool is a powerful utility designed to automatically generate the necessary VRChat assets (FX Controller, Expressions Menu, and Parameters) to control the shader's features in-game. This saves you the time and effort of manually creating animations and menu toggles.
strings.docs.index.li.141: Each feature has a master toggle to enable or disable the entire group.
strings.docs.index.li.142: Within each group, you can select individual controls (e.g., just an "Enable" toggle, or also a "Width" puppet) to save parameter memory.
strings.docs.index.li.143: The "Total Parameter Cost" display at the bottom shows how much of your VRChat parameter budget your selections will use.
strings.docs.index.p.978: This is because the shader is heavily optimized. If a feature is not enabled on the material, its code is completely removed from the shader to save performance. If you generate a menu control for a feature that is disabled on the material, the menu option will appear in-game but will do nothing, because the shader code it's trying to control doesn't exist.
strings.docs.index.p.980: The tool automatically saves your feature and mesh selections for each avatar. When you select an avatar, it will remember the last configuration you generated for it, making it easy to make small changes without starting from scratch.
strings.docs.index.p.1222: The top of the material inspector provides a toolbar with workflow tools that apply to the whole material. Each foldout section in the inspector also has its own Copy, Paste, and Reset buttons.
strings.docs.index.li.883: Lock state is stored on the material itself (a hidden _MaterialLocked property and override tag), so it persists across saves and applies to all targets when editing multiple materials at once.
strings.docs.index.p.983: Presets let you save the entire material state to a JSON file and load it back onto other materials, making it easy to share or reuse a look across your project.
strings.docs.index.p.986: The inspector toolbar includes a search field that live-filters all material properties by name or label as you type. Matching sections auto-expand so you can immediately see (and edit) every hit, making it fast to locate a specific control among the shader's hundreds of properties. Fuzzy matching tolerates typos and partial words, and clearing the box restores the normal foldout layout.
strings.docs.index.p.988: This setting provides a master control to quickly set a performance baseline for different platforms without needing to toggle dozens of individual checkboxes. It adjusts the shader's complexity by disabling the most performance-intensive features at lower levels.
strings.docs.index.li.147: Toon and Stylized PBR lighting modes
strings.docs.index.p.989: When a feature is disabled by a performance level, its controls in the material inspector will be grayed out.
strings.docs.index.p.992: Controls the fundamental rendering behavior of the material.
strings.docs.index.p.995: Fine-tunes the material's render queue position relative to its base render mode. This is essential for resolving z-sorting issues with layered transparent materials like hair, clothing overlays, and accessories.
strings.docs.index.p.997: These controls appear when Render Mode is set to Cutout and Alpha to Coverage is enabled.
strings.docs.index.p.999: Extends the existing Back Face Color feature with support for a completely separate texture and independent emission on back-facing triangles. This is ideal for jacket interiors, capes, double-sided curtains, or any mesh where the inside should look different from the outside.
strings.docs.index.p.1000: This feature incurs zero cost when disabled. The keyword _BACKFACE_TEX_ON is only compiled into the shader when the toggle is active.
strings.docs.index.p.1002: Enables compatibility with Unity's Video Player component and AVPro Video. Video textures often require special handling for gamma correction and UV coordinate flipping that standard textures do not need.
strings.docs.index.p.1004: These controls affect all textures and UV-based effects on the material.
strings.docs.index.p.1006: Animates textures along a vector flow map using two seamlessly crossfading phases, creating continuous directional motion without visible looping — ideal for rivers, conveyor belts, wind streaks, and magic trails.
strings.docs.index.p.1008: Discards geometry per tile of a 4×4 UV grid (0–1 mapped to each 0.25 tile), letting you toggle clothing parts, accessories, or hair pieces on and off from one mesh without blendshapes. Applied consistently across every pass (main color, outline, shadow, depth).
strings.docs.index.p.1010: Warp the UV coordinates using a texture, creating effects like heat haze or water ripples.
strings.docs.index.p.1012: Animates the main texture by treating it as a grid of frames (a spritesheet).
strings.docs.index.p.1014: Procedurally blends randomized texture samples across triangular lattices to completely eliminate repetitive tiling patterns on large surfaces (floors, walls, terrain).
strings.docs.index.p.1016: Makes the material glow with up to 4 independent emission layers. Requires a Bloom post-processing effect in your scene to see the full effect.
strings.docs.index.p.1018: Makes the material glow in response to scene light levels — the less light hits it, the more it glows. Perfect for glow-in-the-dark accents, UV-reactive paint, or emergency-lights that only appear in dark rooms.
strings.docs.index.p.1021: This feature allows you to replace the standard base texture with a procedurally generated pattern. This can reduce texture memory usage and allow for dynamic, animated effects without external texture files.
strings.docs.index.p.1023: This feature allows you to use the generated procedural texture as a mask or input for other shader features, instead of just using it as the base color. This is a powerful way to create complex, dynamic effects by combining procedural patterns with other material properties.
strings.docs.index.p.1227: These controls enable shader-driven animation of time-based effects, offering more precise control than Unity's default time variables.
strings.docs.index.p.1229: A set of controls that affect the final look of the material.
strings.docs.index.p.1025: This setting controls how all colors with "Animate Hue" enabled will change over time.
strings.docs.index.h3.1027: RGBA Color Masking & Global Mask Routing
strings.docs.index.p.1028: Enables 4 independent color zones and emissive channels driven by the RGBA channels of a single mask texture, allowing complete outfit recoloring and cross-module routing from one material.
strings.docs.index.p.1030: Defines 4 global master colors that drive a unified theme across multiple materials on an avatar or prop, so base color, outlines, rim, and emission can all pull from the same shared palette modulated by a single source — much like AudioLink's world theme system, but authored on your own materials.
strings.docs.index.li.152: Direct: The theme colors are used as-is.
strings.docs.index.p.1033: Applies screen-space effects to create retro or stylized looks.
strings.docs.index.p.1035: Uses a texture to mask the material's alpha (visibility), cutting out parts of the surface or restricting the material to specific regions.
strings.docs.index.p.1231: Controls how the material reacts to lights in the scene. This section is disabled if a Surface Style like MatCap (only when its Blend Mode is Override ), Skybox, or Galaxy is chosen, as they provide their own lighting.
strings.docs.index.strong.375: Min Light Brightness / Max Light Brightness:
strings.docs.index.p.1042: Simulates light passing through and scattering within thin or translucent objects, like skin, wax, or leaves. This adds a soft, glowing look from behind the object.
strings.docs.index.p.1044: Creates stretched or elongated specular highlights, common on surfaces with a grain or direction, like brushed metal, hair, or vinyl records.
strings.docs.index.p.1046: Specialized shading models for organic surfaces. These apply regardless of the selected lighting mode.
strings.docs.index.p.1048: Clean, stable anime face shadows using a Signed Distance Field map instead of geometric normals — the standard technique for preventing messy shadow artifacts on stylized faces as the light direction changes.
strings.docs.index.p.1050: Reduces specular shimmer, flickering, and firefly artifacts on dense meshes and detailed normal maps. This is especially valuable in VR headsets where high-frequency specular highlights cause distracting visual noise. Based on the Kaplanyan 2016 technique used in AAA game engines.
strings.docs.index.p.1233: Defines the fundamental appearance of the surface, often overriding standard lighting. Only one style can be active at a time.
strings.docs.index.p.1052: Simulates a refractive, crystalline material. It distorts the view of the texture behind it and can add chromatic aberration for a more stylized look. This effect works best with a base texture enabled.
strings.docs.index.p.1054: Renders a texture that appears to have depth and moves independently of the object's rotation, creating a "window into space" effect. This style disables standard scene lighting.
strings.docs.index.p.1056: Reflects a cubemap from the inside of the object, making it look like a portal or a window into another environment. This style disables standard scene lighting.
strings.docs.index.p.1058: Projects a texture onto the model from the top, front, and side, then blends them together. This is an effective way to texture complex models without needing perfect UV maps, as it avoids stretching and seams.
strings.docs.index.p.1060: A lighting technique that uses a special "material capture" texture to define an object's complete lighting and reflection information. It's a very fast way to get complex, stylized lighting effects. This style disables standard scene lighting.
strings.docs.index.p.1062: A second, independently controlled MatCap layer blended on top of the first for multi-layer material capture looks (e.g. a stylized base layer plus a glossy rim layer).
strings.docs.index.p.1064: Creates a rainbow-like effect where the color shifts based on the viewing angle, similar to a soap bubble or an oil slick. This effect is blended over the existing surface color and lighting.
strings.docs.index.p.1066: Adds an animated, sparkling glitter effect to the surface. This effect is applied after lighting.
strings.docs.index.p.1068: Applies domain-warped fractal Brownian motion (FBM) noise that creates flowing, organic color patterns. The effect is linked to the Global Color Shift timeline for synchronized color animation.
strings.docs.index.p.1070: Renders a volumetric fractal using raymarching techniques. This creates complex, infinite 3D structures that appear to extend infinitely into the object. This style disables standard scene lighting and uses a custom raymarching renderer.
strings.docs.index.p.1074: These properties change based on the selected fractal type:
strings.docs.index.p.1235: These effects are drawn on top of the base surface.
strings.docs.index.p.1077: Overlays a procedural geometric pattern on the surface. This is a powerful feature for creating sci-fi, holographic, or abstract visuals. It has many properties to customize its appearance and animation.
strings.docs.index.p.1083: Allows you to use a texture to mask the grid effect, controlling where it appears on your model. This is useful for restricting the pattern to specific areas without needing to create separate materials.
strings.docs.index.p.1085: Blends a secondary texture over the base material. This is a powerful way to add high-frequency detail, like fabric weaves, scratches, or grunge, without needing a high-resolution base texture.
strings.docs.index.p.1087: Simulates the look of a retro CRT monitor by overlaying a pattern of dark, scrolling lines. This screen-space effect is great for holographic displays, computer terminals, or retro-futuristic aesthetics.
strings.docs.index.p.1089: A simple but effective screen-space effect that darkens every other horizontal row of pixels on the screen. This mimics the look of old interlaced video signals, adding a subtle retro or lo-fi quality to the material.
strings.docs.index.p.1091: Adds a layer of animated noise over the final color, similar to film grain or digital sensor noise. This screen-space effect can be used to add texture, break up smooth gradients, or enhance a lo-fi or cinematic aesthetic. The animation is stepped, not smooth, to better simulate digital noise.
strings.docs.index.p.1093: Simulates a wet surface by darkening the material, boosting its smoothness, and optionally adding animated rain ripples. Great for rainy scenes, recently drenched props, or watery creatures.
strings.docs.index.p.1095: Overlays up to three independent textures onto the surface like stickers or painted emblems, without needing a separate decal projection setup. Each decal layer has its own texture, UV set, blend mode, strength, and rotation, and can be enabled or disabled individually.
strings.docs.index.p.1097: Each of the shader's three decal layers now supports PBR (Physically Based Rendering) overrides. When enabled, a decal can modify the surface's normal map, metallic, and smoothness values in addition to its base color — allowing physically accurate decals like metallic bolts, bumped scars, leather patches, or glossy stickers.
strings.docs.index.p.1098: The PBR overrides are blended using the decal texture's alpha channel multiplied by the decal strength, so they naturally fade at the decal's edges. This feature is available on all three decal layers independently.
strings.docs.index.p.1100: Simulates a sci-fi holographic projection with animated scanlines, a glowing edge rim, and subtle flicker. It is layered over the existing surface color and lighting, making it ideal for projected displays, force-field emitters, and holographic avatars.
strings.docs.index.p.1237: A collection of miscellaneous visual effects.
strings.docs.index.p.1102: Adds a glow to the edges of the object based on the viewing angle (a Fresnel effect). This is great for highlighting silhouettes.
strings.docs.index.p.1104: Creates a visual effect where the material's surface interacts with other objects in the world. This is ideal for force fields, liquid surfaces, or soft proximity indicators. This effect requires the material's Render Mode to be set to Transparent or Additive.
strings.docs.index.p.1106: Adds a pulsing animation to the material's emission strength, creating a "heartbeat" effect.
strings.docs.index.p.1108: Renders a solid outline around the object. The outline will be correctly hidden by effects like Dissolve and Clipping Mask.
strings.docs.index.p.1109: Performance Impact: Outlines can be expensive as they require an additional rendering pass.
strings.docs.index.p.1112: Allows independent stencil testing and writing specifically during the inverted-hull outline pass. This is crucial for preventing outlines from overlapping or dirtying inner face meshes, hair strands, or layered clothing.
strings.docs.index.p.1114: Available when using the FireRat/FireRatShader_Fur BRP or FireRat/FireRatShader_URP_Fur URP master shader variants. Extrudes up to 8 concentric shell layers along vertex normals to render volumetric fur, velvet, and plush textures.
strings.docs.index.p.1116: Creates a concentric ripple effect that distorts vertices and color, emanating from a point in the object's UV space.
strings.docs.index.p.1118: Applies pre-baked vertex animation from a texture instead of a Skinned Mesh Renderer. Each row of the texture is a frame of the animation. Useful for pre-baked cloth, fluids, destruction, or any heavily animated mesh that needs to stay performant.
strings.docs.index.p.1120: Quantizes vertex positions to a coarse grid to emulate the classic wobbly PlayStation 1 aesthetic. Great for retro-styled avatars and worlds, especially combined with pixelation and affine-style textures.
strings.docs.index.p.1122: Dynamically rotates mesh vertices so the object always faces the active camera — useful for sprites, eye highlights, floating companions, and particles that should never be seen edge-on. Applied consistently in shadow, depth, and motion-vector passes.
strings.docs.index.p.1124: URP Only Provides true screen-space refraction for glass, water, and crystal-like materials by sampling the camera's opaque texture with UV offsets derived from the surface normal. This creates realistic distortion of the background scene visible through transparent geometry.
strings.docs.index.p.1126: Animates the emission intensity over time using various waveform patterns, creating pulsing, breathing, or flashing glow effects without requiring any animation controllers or scripts.
strings.docs.index.p.1128: Allows per-vertex control over the outline thickness using a texture map. This enables artistic effects like thicker outlines on silhouette edges and thinner outlines on interior details.
strings.docs.index.p.1129: This control appears within the Outline settings when Outline is enabled.
strings.docs.index.p.1239: Effects designed to create digital distortion and glitch aesthetics.
strings.docs.index.p.1131: Displaces the model's vertices in various patterns to create a glitchy shape animation. Each mode has unique properties for Strength, Speed, and other controls.
strings.docs.index.p.1133: Applies a flickering effect to the material's color using different patterns. Strength controls how dark the flicker gets.
strings.docs.index.p.1135: Causes the Glitch Flicker effect to also affect the material's transparency, creating see-through glitches. This is a sub-option of Glitch Flicker.
strings.docs.index.p.1241: Effects used to make a material appear or disappear.
strings.docs.index.p.1137: Triggers visual surface transformations when approaching or moving away from a reference position (the active VR camera / player head, the object pivot, or a custom world position).
strings.docs.index.li.153: Camera / Player: Distance is calculated to the VR camera / player's head.
strings.docs.index.li.154: Object Pivot: Distance is calculated to the object's transform origin.
strings.docs.index.li.155: Dissolve / Fade: Fades out alpha transparency smoothly.
strings.docs.index.li.156: Dither Transparency: Clips surface pixels using a screen-door dither pattern.
strings.docs.index.p.1139: Fades the object out with a Bayer-matrix screen-door stipple instead of alpha blending. Dithered cutouts behave like opaque geometry, so they avoid transparency sorting artifacts — ideal for transparent fabrics, hair, and cross-fades in VR.
strings.docs.index.p.1141: Masks out a specific color from the final output, creating a green-screen or blue-screen effect. Useful for live streaming overlays, video production, or creative transparency effects.
strings.docs.index.p.1143: Fades the object out based on its distance from the camera. Useful for level-of-detail (LOD) systems.
strings.docs.index.p.1145: Fades the object out when the camera gets too close, preventing transparent materials from filling the view or clipping through the player's head in VR.
strings.docs.index.p.1147: Makes the object appear or disappear using a procedural pattern, often with a glowing edge.
strings.docs.index.p.1151: Reveals the object with a smooth, directional wipe across its surface. Great for dramatic entrances.
strings.docs.index.p.1153: Animates the model's vertices collapsing into its center point, as if being sucked into a black hole.
strings.docs.index.p.1155: Automatically disables expensive shader effects when the object is far from the camera, providing a significant performance boost for distant objects without requiring Unity LOD Groups. The transition is smooth and configurable.
strings.docs.index.p.1156: Effects controlled by the LOD system include procedural textures, overlays, surface styles, and other expensive per-pixel operations. Core rendering (base texture, lighting, normal maps) is always preserved regardless of distance.
strings.docs.index.p.1243: Low-level controls for rendering and performance.
strings.docs.index.p.1158: Uses a height map to create the illusion of depth and relief on a flat surface. This can add significant detail without extra geometry, but can be performance-intensive.
strings.docs.index.p.1160: Uses a texture to perform a hard clip on the material, making parts of it invisible. Unlike transparency, this is an all-or-nothing effect that works in any render mode.
strings.docs.index.p.1163: Controls from which cameras the material is rendered. Useful for hiding parts from mirrors, showing elements only in VR headset eyes, or creating desktop/stream-exclusive effects. Enforced consistently across the main pass as well as shadow, depth-normals, depth-only, and motion-vector passes.
strings.docs.index.strong.909: painter's masking tape applied pixel-by-pixel onto the screen
strings.docs.index.p.1165: Out of the box, the default settings ( Comp = Always , Pass = Keep ) do nothing—the shader simply renders normally on every pixel. But when configured, it allows materials on different objects to communicate with each other visually without touching C# code.
strings.docs.index.li.157: The main character writes Ref = 2 , Pass = Replace when visible.
strings.docs.index.li.158: An X-Ray outline material sets Ref = 2 , Comp = NotEqual . When occluded behind a wall, it draws the glowing silhouette only where the main body isn't directly visible.

strings.docs.index.td.164: What to do if the stencil test fails ( Fail ) or depth/wall test fails ( ZFail ).
strings.docs.index.p.1169: If you want to create a magic portal window:
strings.docs.index.p.1171: Advanced hardware-level rendering controls for specialized effects and workflows. These settings directly control GPU pipeline state and should be used with care.
strings.docs.index.p.1173: Sets the material's VRCFallback override tag, which controls which standard shader VRChat swaps in when custom shaders are blocked by safety settings (e.g. when a viewer hides custom shaders or on incompatible platforms).
strings.docs.index.p.1174: Picking a fallback that matches your render mode keeps the avatar looking reasonable instead of flashing white for users with custom shaders hidden.
strings.docs.index.p.1176: A texture-driven mask that controls where HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) color adjustments are applied. This allows selective color grading on specific parts of the material while leaving other areas untouched.
strings.docs.index.p.1178: Enables real-time in-viewport inspection of intermediate lighting and shading buffers for debugging material setups and spotting rendering issues.
strings.docs.index.li.174: DirectShading — Direct scene light attenuation and cel shadow mask.
strings.docs.index.li.175: Roughness / GI — Surface roughness and indirect diffuse irradiance.
strings.docs.index.li.177: AudioLink — Live AudioLink 4-band spectrum diagnostic visualization.
strings.docs.index.li.178: TexelDensity — World-space UV texel density checkerboard to identify stretching or over/under-sampling.
strings.docs.index.li.179: Complexity — Heatmap visualization of active feature complexity.
strings.docs.index.p.1181: In addition to dedicated visualizers, many built-in shader effects feature integrated AudioLink modulation toggles. When enabled, the effect's intensity, speed, or displacement scales proportionally with the amplitude of a chosen frequency band.
strings.docs.index.p.1184: Global controls that shape how every AudioLink reading responds to audio. They apply to all per-feature links and both visualizers.
strings.docs.index.td.184: No temporal smoothing. Visualizers read the live AudioLink frame directly (identical to the original behavior).
strings.docs.index.td.185: Zero overhead — no extra texture lookups or math.
strings.docs.index.td.186: Two samples per tap. Negligible cost.
strings.docs.index.td.187: One extra texture sample per tap. The CRT asset auto-updates on the GPU each frame while it exists.
strings.docs.index.strong.811: Assets → Create → Rendering → Custom Render Texture
strings.docs.index.li.927: All FireRatShader variants across both render pipelines — BRP ( FireRatShader , FireRatShader_Fur , FireRatShader_TwoPass ) and URP ( FireRatShader_URP , FireRatShader_URP_Fur , FireRatShader_URP_TwoPass ) — expose identical temporal-smoothing controls.
strings.docs.index.td.192: Renders discrete vertical equalizer bars resembling physical DJ mixer displays or studio graphic equalizers. Each bar samples an averaged frequency sub-band with configurable spacing and edge anti-aliasing.
strings.docs.index.td.193: Traces a smooth, continuous mathematical FFT frequency curve with 3-tap neighbor smoothing. Includes an optional semi-transparent filled area underneath the curve.
strings.docs.index.td.194: Transforms the frequency spectrum into a 360-degree circular radar display radiating outward from the center point, creating an energetic glowing aura, circular ring gauge, or techno-shield.
strings.docs.index.td.195: Displays a continuous temporal history heatmap of audio frequencies over time. Frequencies run horizontally while time scrolls vertically, creating a rich visual soundscape spectrogram.
strings.docs.index.td.200: Simulates an authentic cathode-ray tube (CRT) or digital laser oscilloscope. Draws a vibrant neon beam tracing the audio voltage over time, complete with a sharp inner core and exponential outer bloom glow.
strings.docs.index.td.201: Renders a solid bipolar audio waveform filled symmetrically from the center line (Y = 0.5), similar to visualizers in modern digital audio workstations (DAWs) and SoundCloud waveforms.
strings.docs.index.td.202: Wraps the time-domain waveform into a 360-degree circular loop around a center point. The ring pulses and distorts radially in response to incoming audio waves.
strings.docs.index.td.203: Deforms the 3D model's actual geometry in the vertex shader, displacing vertices along their surface normals in real-time based on the local audio waveform value. Ideal for audio-reactive speakers, pulsating orbs, and dancing avatar elements.
strings.docs.index.li.204: Mono: Summed average of Left and Right audio channels (L + R) * 0.5 .
strings.docs.index.li.205: Left: Samples only the discrete Left stereo channel.
strings.docs.index.li.206: Right: Samples only the discrete Right stereo channel.
strings.docs.index.p.1197: Both the Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform visualizers provide a consistent suite of color, coordinate projection, spatial transformation, and blending options.
strings.docs.index.p.1200: The visualizers can be projected onto the surface using several coordinate frames:
strings.docs.index.li.934: In Unity, shader variants and features are enabled via shader keywords (e.g. _METALLICGLOSSMAP_ON , _USE_EMISSION_ON , _RENDER_MODE_CUTOUT ). When materials are imported from external .unitypackage files, upgraded across shader versions, or animated by Unity Animation Clips and VRChat FX layers, serialized keywords in .mat files can become stale or desynchronized from the actual material properties.
strings.docs.index.li.941: Automates converting avatar materials from Poiyomi (Free/Pro), lilToon, Unity Standard, and UTS shaders to FireRatShader.
strings.docs.index.li.942: Automatically remaps diffuse albedo, bump/normal maps, metallic/smoothness/roughness, primary & secondary emission maps, toon shade thresholds, ramp textures, and inverted-hull outline settings.
strings.docs.index.li.943: Supports converting individual materials or batch-converting an entire avatar hierarchy, with optional non-destructive backup copy creation.
strings.docs.index.li.946: Spawns an in-editor simulation rig with an audio source and spectrum analyzer, allowing you to preview, tune, and test all audio-reactive features (pulses, spectrum visualizers, waveforms, audio-driven glitter) directly inside the Unity Editor without entering Play Mode or launching VRChat.
strings.docs.index.li.949: Scans any avatar or scene hierarchy and aggregates all unique FireRat materials into a single batch inspector.
strings.docs.index.li.950: Allows editing common properties simultaneously across clothing, accessories, body, and hair (e.g. bulk performance level toggling, light mode adjustments, render mode changes, and batch material locking/optimizing).
strings.docs.index.li.951: Provides a 1-click batch pipeline converter to instantly switch all avatar materials between BRP and URP master variants.
strings.docs.index.h3.1211: Sprite Sheet & Flipbook Importer (with Animated GIF Converter)
strings.docs.index.li.956: Bakes high-end PC avatar shader composites (diffuse, decals, recolor masks, glitter, matcaps, and emission) down into lightweight mobile textures.
strings.docs.index.li.957: Automatically creates a duplicate Quest avatar material set targeting mobile-optimized shaders or FireRat Low tier with 100% texture consistency.
strings.docs.index.p.1214: The material inspector is localized via community-maintained JSON translation packs in Assets/FireRatShader/Languages/ . A language dropdown at the top of the inspector switches all section headers, property labels, and tooltips instantly.
strings.switcher.label: Language
